1.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made]
A cubit is 46 centimeters. Alternate translation: [20 cubits … 10 cubits] or [9.2 meters … 4.6 meters]

2.q: ten cubits … five cubits … thirty cubits
2.note: A cubit is 46 centimeters. Alternate translation: [4.6 meters … 2.3 meters … 13.8 meters]
This refers to a tank or basin that would hold water.
This is metal that was melted then formed in a mold.
Alternate translation: [from one edge to the other]
Circumference is the distance or measurement around a circular object or area.

3.note: A cubit is 46 centimeters. Alternate translation: [every 46 centimeters]

3.q: when the sea itself was cast
3.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when the workers cast the sea itself]

4.note: This refers to the tank or basin that held water for sacrifices.
Alternate translation: [was on top of twelve oxen]
These are images of oxen made of bronze. Alternate translation: [twelve large figures of bulls] or [twelve bronze oxen]

4.q: “The Sea” was set on top of them
4.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers set ‘The Sea’ on top of the oxen]
This is the back quarter of the body of an animal with four feet.

5.q: thick as the width of a hand
its brim was forged like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom
5.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers forged the brim to look like the brim of a cup, to curve outward like a lily]
“3,000 baths.” A bath is a unit of volume equal to about 22 liters. Alternate translation: [66 kiloliters] (See also: [Biblical Volume](ta:translate-bvolume))

6.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made … they put]

6.q: items used in performing the burnt offering were to be washed in them
6.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people were to wash the items used in performing the burnt offering in them]

7.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made … they placed]

7.q: that were made from the instructions for their design
7.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [according to the instructions for their design] or [according to how Solomon instructed his workers to design them]

7.q: on the right hand … on the left
7.note: Alternate translation: [on the right side … on the left side] or [on the south side … on the north side]

8.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made … They made]

9.q: he made the courtyard … and overlaid
9.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made … they overlaid … They placed]

10.note: Here “he” refers to Solomon. The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [They placed]

10.q: on the east side of the temple, facing toward the south
10.note: Alternate translation: [next to the southeast corner of the temple]

11.note: See how you translated this name in 2 Chronicles 2:13.
bowls that held blood that was used in the house of God for sprinkling the altar

11.q: Huram finished the work that he did
11.note: Here Huram represents all who worked on the temple. Alternate translation: [Huram and the other workers finished the work that they did]

12.note: The upper part of a pillar is called a capital. See how you translated “capital” in 2 Chronicles 3:15. Alternate translation: [bowl-shaped tops] or [bowl-shaped upper parts]
This refers to the decorative carving or markings on the upper part of the pillars. Alternate translation: [carvings that resembled chains]

13.note: Here Huram represents all who worked on the temple. Alternate translation: [Huram and the other workers had made]
“the 400 pomegranates.” Translate “pomegranates” as you did in 2 Chronicles 3:16.

14.note: Here Huram, who is also called Huram-Abi, represents all those who worked with him. Alternate translation: [They also made]

15.q: one sea and the twelve bulls
15.note: This is a large decorative washing container. Translate “sea” as you did in 2 Chronicles 4:2 and “bulls” as you did in 2 Chronicles 4:3.

16.note: Here Huram, who is also called Huram-Abi, represents all those who worked with him. Alternate translation: [Huram-Abi and his craftsmen made]
Alternate translation: [other tools] or [other objects used for the altar]
Bronze that the workmen polished so that it would reflect light.

17.note: The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [The king commanded his workers to cast them]
This is the name of a city.

18.note: The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made] or [Solomon had his workers make]

18.q: the weight of the bronze could not be known
18.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This could mean: (1) there was so much bronze no one tried to weigh it. Alternate translation: [no one even tried to weigh the bronze] or (2) this is a hyperbole that emphasizes the great amount of bronze. Alternate translation: [no one could even determine how much all the bronze weighed] (See also: [Hyperbole](ta:figs-hyperbole))

19.note: The readers should understand that Solomon probably commanded other people to do the actual work. Alternate translation: [Solomon’s workers made]
This refers to all of the bowls and tools that were used in the house of God.

19.q: the tables on which the bread of the presence was to be placed
19.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the tables on which the priests were to place the bread of the presence]
This is a reference to the 12 loaves of bread that were placed in front of the altar. See how you translated this in 2 Chronicles 2:4.

21.note: The “flowers” and “lamps” were part of the lampstands.
This is a tool made from two sticks of wood or metal connected at one end and used for picking up objects.

22.q: Also the lamp trimmers … were all made of pure gold
22.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The workers also made the lamp trimmers … out of pure gold]
These would have been used to trim the wicks of the lamps.

22.q: its inner doors … were made of gold
22.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the workers made its inner doors … out of gold]
